newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa loses ground after choppy trade.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa loses ground after choppy trade.

text.p: London cocoa futures ended weaker on Thursday after see-sawing with fund and origin sales countered by trade and industry buying.
A hefty 4,800 lots of AAs said to have been struck by Cargill to Phibro in the morning session accounted for much of the day's turnover of 8,269 lots, traders said.
"There were more of those in the afternoon," said one trader.
Benchmark March cocoa lost seven stg on the day to stand at 905 stg a tonne, just off a session low of 904. Other contracts, except spot December, were five down to four up.
Traders said the AA deal could be related to a large amount of physical cocoa believed to be held by one trader after taking delivery in September.
The bulk of this will have to be re-graded for any re-delivery to the futures market and some traders said the owner could want to dispose of it in the physical market instead.
Futures' inability to follow up gains after Wednesday's recovery from a nine-month low of 899 stg disappointed the longs, lending credence to the view that another test of lows was possible.
But contracts were underpinned by sterling which lost some ground against the dollar, trading around $1.6630 against Wednesday's close of $1.6722.

Technically, cocoa faces strong overhead resistance starting from 917 stg. The current trading range has been extended to 899-956 stg, but a downtrend line coming in around 937 stg is likely to put on heavy pressure, analysts said.
Nearby support is the contract low of 899.
